newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP Escondida copper costs US$0.44/pound.
newsitem.headline: BHP Escondida copper costs US$0.44/pound.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co (BHP) said on Monday its cash costs at the giant Escondida copper mine in Chile were averaging 44 U.S. cents per pound.
The company is aiming to reduce costs below that level through its next phase of development over 18 months, Jim Lewis, executive general manager of BHP copper, told a briefing.
BHP plans to expand its 57.5 percent-owned Escondida mine in stages and is looking at its Norte and Carmen desposits near Escondida for growth as well, Lewsis said.
"One of Escondidia's strengths over the past few years has been its ability to continually expand," Lewis said.
Increases throughput of ore at the mine would not necessarily translate into higher prodution copper as ore grades at Escondida are in natural decline, Lewis said.

At 44 cents, Escondida ranks amongh the world's lowest cost producers and compares favourably with costs at other BHP mines and with those of some producers in Australia, where costs can run as high as the mid-70-cents-a-pound range, analysts said.
Copper currently feteches about US$1.11 a pound.
Earlier on Monday, Lewis said average cost of producing refined copper cathodes for BHP was 57 U.S. cents a pound.
BHP is the world's second largest copper producer behind Chile's Codelco.
